extracted.intended_audience: general public, stakeholders, license applicants, and others seeking an overview of the NRC's role and structure
extracted.subtask_description: High-level description of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission: its mission, legal foundation, organizational components, and primary regulatory objectives for civilian uses of nuclear materials and facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary mission — licensing and regulation to protect health and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission licenses and regulates civilian use of nuclear energy to protect public health and safety and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement defines the NRC's central purpose and the primary evaluative lens for its activities: protection of public health, safety, and the environment when licensing or regulating civilian nuclear uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal foundation — establishment and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) was established as an independent regulatory agency under the provisions of the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974 (42 U.S.C. 5801 et seq.) and Executive Order 11834 of January 15, 1975.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the statutory and executive-order basis for NRC authority and independence; useful for understanding the legal context and limits of NRC actions and rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical transfer of functions
rubrics_metrics.description: All licensing and related regulatory functions formerly assigned to the Atomic Energy Commission were transferred to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains continuity of regulatory responsibilities and may inform interpretation of historical regulatory approaches, precedents, and records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational program components
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's major program components are the Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards, the Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation, the Office of Nuclear Security and Incident Response, and the Office of Nuclear Regulatory Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the principal NRC offices responsible for different regulatory domains; useful for directing comments, petitions, or inquiries to the appropriate program office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory objectives and statutory consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission ensures that the civilian uses of nuclear materials and facilities are conducted in a manner consistent with the public health and safety, environmental quality, national security, and the antitrust laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the substantive objectives and legal domains the NRC must consider and be consistent with when regulating — public health & safety, environmental quality, national security, and antitrust law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and administrative footprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Headquarters offices are located in suburban Maryland, and there are four regional offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes NRC's physical/organizational presence, which can affect regional jurisdiction, point-of-contact, and where regional issues may be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary focus area — electric power generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the Commission's effort is focused on regulating the use of nuclear energy to generate electric power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the predominant subject matter of NRC regulation and programmatic effort, helpful for stakeholders to gauge relevance of NRC activities to specific nuclear-sector interests.
